newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH AIR INDUSTRY CAUTIOUS AT SCHIPHOL BAN RULING.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH AIR INDUSTRY CAUTIOUS AT SCHIPHOL BAN RULING.

text.p: The Dutch airline industry had a cautious attitude to a court judgement on Friday to postpone a night take-off ban at Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport for a further week.
A Haarlem court ruled that pending more investigations its final judgement has been postponed till next Friday, August 15, and that the ban cannot continue until a decision is reached.

Schiphol introduced a night ban on August 5 on aircraft such as the McDonnell Douglas DC-10 and the Boeing 747 in its 100, 200, 300 and SP versions in a bid to keep within government imposed noise limits.
But the court ruled the airport cannot continue with the ban and if it does so it faces a fine ranging from one million to 10 million guilders.
Dutch airline Martinair and the Dutch air transport association (ATAN) and El Al, all brought court actions against the Dutch airport and the government in a bid to overturn the ban.

Martinair sought a court order to exempt its Boeing 747-200 flights as it argued that they meet so-called low-noise Chapter 3 standards and an airline spokesman said it now remains cautious about the final outcome.
"The court appears to have given the industry the benefit of the doubt and feels that Schiphol has not been realistic," he added
Hans Knuvers, spokesman for ATAN, added: "This could be termed a small success but the industry will have to just wait and see."

ATAN and ground handling firm Aero Groundservices(AGS) had attempted to get the ban postponed until at least January 1, 1998. ATAN argued this would give airlines time to reschedule services and advise their customers.

El Al and the Long Beach-based, Polar Air Cargo, backed the position of ATAN and AGS. Industry sources said these two carriers will be the worst affected, while AGS is the cargo handler for both airlines. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
